territorial_scope.description: Applies to elections in Arizona and to persons and publications within the State, as defined in the new section.

evidence.quote: MEANS ANY ELECTION IN THIS STATE, INCLUDING A PRIMARY, PRESIDENTIAL PREFERENCE, SPECIAL OR GENERAL ELECTION.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Creates a civil cause of action in Arizona for 'digital impersonation': deceptive AI-generated synthetic media that replaces or simulates a person's likeness or voice without consent. Plaintiffs may seek declaratory relief and, in limited cases, injunctive relief and damages. Applies fourteen days after the section's effective date.
summary.long: Adds A.R.S. § 16-1023 creating a civil action for 'digital impersonation': deceptive AI-generated synthetic media that replaces or simulates a person's likeness or voice without consent. Ballot candidates for public or party office and any Arizona citizen may sue within two years of knowing of publication, proving non-consensual publication and either no reasonable conveyance of inauthenticity or non-obviousness to a reasonable person. Paid-advertisement claims lie only against the originator, orderer, placer or payer; interactive computer service providers are shielded for third-party content. Preliminary declaratory relief requires clear and convincing evidence plus one additional element, such as an election within 180 days, a sexual or criminal depiction, or significant personal, financial or reputational harm; court rules within two days, excluding weekends and court holidays. Injunctive relief and damages require further proof, including a sexual depiction, non-public-figure status and actual knowledge or failure to take corrective action within 21 days. Unserved defendants are dismissed after 90 days. Parents or guardians may sue for minors or incapacitated persons. The section must be narrowly construed to protect public discourse and artistic expression, and contested actions for permanent relief or damages carry a jury right. It applies fourteen days after the section's effective date.

relations.target_text: Arizona Revised Statutes, Title 16, Chapter 7, Article 1 (adds Section 16-1023)
relations.note: The act amends this title and article by adding one new section, 16-1023. No other statute is amended, repealed or implemented in the text.

evidence.quote: TITLE 16, CHAPTER 7, ARTICLE 1, ARIZONA REVISED STATUTES, IS AMENDED BY ADDING SECTION 16-1023, TO READ:

notes: Only one relation is stated: the amendment of ARS Title 16, Chapter 7, Article 1. The text cites no other instrument; its defined terms in subsection Q.3 and Q.4 are self-contained, and 'interactive computer service' appears in subsection C without an external reference. Timing is internally unreconciled: subsection P says the section applies fourteen days after the effective date, while Sec. 2 declares the act an emergency measure operative immediately. The title says 'relating to prohibited acts', but the new section creates a cause of action and remedies rather than a prohibition.

thresholds.variable_text: days before election for which the candidate's relief request is made (election scheduled within this window)
thresholds.value_text: WITHIN ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY DAYS OF THE DATE THAT THE RELIEF IS REQUESTED
thresholds.measurement: Measured from the date the preliminary declaratory relief is requested to the date an election is scheduled for the office in question
thresholds.consequence: Preliminary declaratory relief may be granted only if the plaintiff proves the subsection A elements and at least one additional element; a scheduled election within 180 days of the request is one such element.
thresholds.conditions: Applies only to a plaintiff who is a candidate for public office or political party office; must be combined with the subsection A elements.

evidence.quote: THE PERSON IS A CANDIDATE FOR PUBLIC OFFICE OR POLITICAL PARTY OFFICE AND AN ELECTION IS SCHEDULED TO BE HELD FOR THAT PUBLIC OFFICE OR POLITICAL PARTY OFFICE WITHIN ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY DAYS OF THE DATE THAT THE RELIEF IS REQUESTED.

thresholds.variable_text: days after publisher's actual knowledge within which reasonable corrective action must be taken
thresholds.value_text: FAILED TO TAKE REASONABLE CORRECTIVE ACTION WITHIN TWENTY-ONE DAYS AFTER THE PUBLISHER HAD ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE
thresholds.measurement: Measured from the time the publisher has actual knowledge that the recording or image is a digital impersonation
thresholds.consequence: Injunctive relief and damages are available only if the publisher failed to take reasonable corrective action within this period; reasonable corrective action includes removing or disabling access and publishing a statement to the same audience.
thresholds.conditions: Applies only where the digital impersonation depicts a sexual act or nudity, the plaintiff was not a public figure, and the statutory elements of subsection I are proven.

evidence.quote: THE PUBLISHER FAILED TO TAKE REASONABLE CORRECTIVE ACTION WITHIN TWENTY-ONE DAYS AFTER THE PUBLISHER HAD ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE THAT THE RECORDING OR IMAGE WAS A DIGITAL IMPERSONATION.
